title: Recover missed keepalive chunks and align token ledgers across reconnects
creator: Avery Collins
description:
Summary:
Keepalive frames emitted by some clients/proxies occasionally carry partial token output (prompt echoes, small completions) and are treated by intermediate proxies as non‑semantic traffic. In our streaming metering pipeline these keepalive fragments are sometimes dropped or timestamped incorrectly during reconnects, causing either undercharging (missed credits) or duplicate charging after resume. This ticket designs and implements a robust handling and reconciliation path for keepalive fragments so that final token tallies are correct across reconnects and proxy edgecases.

Observed behavior / impact:
- Repro (internal): flaky reproduction on mobile client behind gRPC HTTP proxies that inject 1–3 byte keepalive pings. If proxy strips or reorders those frames and the client reconnects, server-side fragment ledger shows a gap and later resume attaches a second finalization fragment, leading to either missing credits or double-crediting depending on ordering.
- Customer impact: medium-to-high for bursty mobile apps; noticeable billing mismatches in high-volume customers (support tickets).
- Incidents: support ticket #SUP-9812 and internal telemetry spike on 2026-02-28 (billing-reconcile job reported ~0.2% token delta on streaming sessions).

Design proposal (high level):
1) Treat keepalive fragments as "provisional fragments" with deterministic fragment IDs derived from session_id + monotonic fragment_index so they can be deduped across reconnects.
2) Add a small header field in the streaming protocol: fragment_type: keepalive | output | finalization and fragment_index to ensure ordering even if timestamps are noisy. New headers are backward-compatible - servers will ignore unknown headers and clients can fall back.
3) Ledger changes: mark provisional fragments as provisional credits and do not commit to billing until a finalization fragment or an expiry watermark (session idle > 30s) is observed.
4) Reconciliation path: on reconnect, caller provides last_acknowledged_fragment_index; the server will attempt to reconcile provisional fragments by comparing deterministic IDs and either commit or discard duplicates. A reconciliation job will scan sessions with provisional fragments older than 5m and apply corrections (commit once we can prove finality, or refund/void provisional credits).
5) Metric/alerting: add new counters for provisional_fragment_count, provisional_commit_rate, provisional_double_detected, and reconcile_corrections_per_hour. Create dashboard and an SLO for reconcile delay (target < 2min median).

Implementation tasks:
- protocol: add fragment_type and fragment_index to streaming wire spec and update SDKs (JS/Go/Python) to include them where available. (ENG+SDK collaboration)
- server: deterministic fragment ID generation, provisional flag in shard-ledger, commit-on-finalization logic, and reconciliation job. Add unit + e2e tests simulating reorders and proxy drops.
- billing: ensure reporter for billing pipeline treats provisional entries specially (do not emit final invoice rows until commit).
- infra: add feature-flag gated rollout and migration script to backfill recent sessions with provisional state.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulated tests that previously demonstrated under/overcharging now show identical token tallies before and after reconnects across 10k randomized runs.
- No customer-visible double charges in a canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 48 hours.
- Dashboard shows provisional_commit_rate > 99% within 2 minutes and reconcile_corrections trending to zero.
- SDKs gracefully fall back when fragment_index/header absent.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Increasing wire header size: minimal (two small fields). Older clients will still work but will generate more provisional fragments; reconciliation may need to be conservative to avoid refunds.
- Performance: additional ledger writes for provisional state; mitigate via batching and memtable coalescing.
- Complexity: adds lifecycle state to fragments that affects billing pipeline; requires careful testing across failover scenarios.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/KEEPALIVE-METERING (internal)
- Repro harness: https://git.redwood.ai/redwood/metering/repros/keepalive-repro
- Draft PR (protocol headers): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7891
- Draft PR (ledger + reconcile): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7898

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on ledger invariants and idempotency of commit/void flows.
- Security: provisional tokens are sensitive for billing; ensure reconcile job auth is tightly controlled.
- UX: Console shows provisional tokens in session trace with gray stripe; product has approved minimal UI changes (see console-UX PR).
comments: 2026-03-06 - Diego Martinez: Ran repro harness across proxy variants (env: staging-proxy-a, staging-proxy-b). Confirmed keepalive frames sometimes dropped, leaving provisional fragments in ledger. Captured packet traces and uploaded to repro artifact. Next: implement deterministic fragment_id prototype.

2026-03-08 - Avery Collins: Design review with billing and SDK teams. Agreed on fragment_index + fragment_type wire contract. Billing requested a conservative expiry of 5m for provisional entries for initial rollout. SDKs asked for graceful fallback for older clients.

2026-03-10 - Diego Martinez: Implemented server-side deterministic fragment ID and provisional flag. Added unit tests for dedupe logic. Draft PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7898

2026-03-12 - Priya Nair (Billing): Reviewed ledger changes. Requested explicit audit trail entries for provisional->committed transitions. Added as follow-up task to ensure accounting exports include reconciliation tags.

2026-03-14 - Diego Martinez: Started canary rollout (feature flag metering.keepalive_reconcile = true) to 2% traffic. Monitoring provisional_commit_rate metric. No anomalous billing spikes in first 6 hours. Next: expand to 10% if steady.
